basis: Small-intestinal stasis and bacterial overgrowth cause malabsorption; osteoporosis and nephrolithiasis are downstream, separately diagnosed complications.
Carcinoma originates in breast ducts; breast has no axis. Metastatic organ involvement is not intrinsic across this umbrella.
Arachnodactyly, joint laxity and spondylolisthesis define a skeletal and joint disorder.
P5CS-deficiency-associated spastic paraplegia; permanent pes cavus is frequent (30-79%). Ocular, hearing and urinary findings are below 30%.
Squamous carcinoma arises in breast parenchyma, outside the axes; squamous histology does not establish skin origin.
Genetic photodermatosis with chronic cutaneous damage; keratitis is frequent (30-79%), supporting direct ocular involvement.
Reactive lymphoid follicular hyperplasia produces immune-mediated disease of small-airway walls; associated systemic diseases are not assumed.
Bartonella infection with regional lymphadenitis; inoculation papules are transient. Ocular, hepatic, skeletal and neurologic complications are below 30%.
Autoimmune disease defined by lupus-specific skin lesions; associated systemic lupus is a separate diagnosis.
Progressive degeneration of choroid, retinal pigment epithelium and retina; ocular vascular changes remain within the ocular axis.
Human strongylid infections predominantly involve intestinal nematodes, especially hookworms; pulmonary and CNS sites depend on subtype.
Glycine metabolism disorder defined by encephalopathy, seizures and developmental impairment; hyperglycinuria does not establish renal damage.
Glycoprotein metabolism disorder; direct neurodevelopmental impairment is common across congenital glycosylation/deglycosylation disorders (>30%); other organs vary.
Familial vesicoureteral reflux directly affects the bladder-ureter urinary tract; infection is a separate complication.
Named malformation combines frontonasal skeletal defects with cloacal exstrophy involving the bladder and hindgut; additional organs are unspecified.
B-cell lymphoma is a blood-cell malignancy and lymphoma mechanism; mediastinal location alone does not establish lung involvement.
Non-syndromic uterine and fallopian-tube malformation lies outside the axes; associated urinary malformations are separate anomalies.
Separation of vitreous from retina is confined to the eye; inherited-neurologic ancestry does not establish extraocular disease.
Autoimmune superficial blistering and erosive skin disease; oral mucosal involvement is uncommon, below 30%.
Hypospadias is a congenital abnormality of the urethral opening; the urethra belongs to the renal axis.
Intellectual disability, epilepsy, spasticity and hemiplegia define neurologic disease; muscle stiffness reflects neurologic dysfunction.
PKD2-associated renal cystic disease; hepatic cysts occur in 6/8 (~75%), indicating direct cystic involvement. Secondary hypertension is separately diagnosed.
Astrocytoma originates in the cerebral hemispheres; optic-tract involvement belongs to a narrower child concept.
Developmental impairment, digital skeletal anomalies and dental/palatal malformations are defining features; cardiac, renal and hearing findings lack common frequencies.
Developmental impairment and seizures define the syndrome; retinal/skin pigment disorders are explicitly definitional despite <30% HPO rates. Infections alone do not prove immune deficiency.
